name: Ivchenko-Progress / Motor Sich

header.one_liner: Ukrainian engine design bureau (Ivchenko-Progress, Zaporizhzhia) and its production partner Motor Sich — designer/producer of the AI-20 turboprop that powers the IAF's An-32 fleet. Compact card: Ukraine engine supplier whose India footprint is the An-32 AI-20 engine dependency, disrupted by the war.

what_it_is.prose: Ivchenko-Progress (State Enterprise Ivchenko-Progress, Zaporizhzhia) is Ukraine's principal aero-engine design bureau, and Motor Sich is its long-standing serial-production partner in the same city. Together they are the designer and producer of the Ivchenko AI-20 turboprop, the AI-20D variant of which powers the Indian Air Force's Antonov An-32 fleet (two engines per aircraft). India's exposure to these Ukrainian firms is therefore the An-32's engine dependency: AI-20 engine supply, spares and overhaul. This dependency was severely disrupted by the Russia-Ukraine war, which is a key reason India shifted to an indigenous An-32 overhaul route — including indigenised AI-20 engine overhaul at No. 1 BRD Kanpur. This is a compact (Tier C) card: as a foreign engine supplier, the firms' documented India footprint is essentially the An-32 AI-20 engine link, and there is limited additional India-specific public evidence (no Indian orders, JVs or production).

variant: Tier C compact card (An-32 engine supplier)
open_questions: Extent of any residual Ukrainian AI-20 engine/spares support to India during the war is unclear.
How fully India can indigenise AI-20 engine overhaul (vs airframe/avionics) is not publicly detailed.
